## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature and SuttaCentral)
*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and SuttaCentral data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*
The *Kūṭavinicchayikapetavatthu* (Pv 34) is a poem in the canonical *Petavatthu* collection of the Pali Khuddaka Nikāya [SuttaCentral]. The narrative examines the spiritual and karmic dangers associated with lying, malicious gossip, and divisive speech [SuttaCentral]. In his survey of Pali literature, K. R. Norman identifies the opening and concluding half-verses of the *Kūṭavinicchayikapetavatthu* as narrative or structural additions intended to frame the circumstances of the poem [Norman 1983].
No cross-language parallels in Sanskrit, Chinese, or Tibetan are identified by SuttaCentral or DharmaNexus [SuttaCentral; DharmaNexus]. Within Pali literature, DharmaNexus records extensive text reuse between the verses (§§1.1–8.4) and their commentary in the *Petavatthu-aṭṭhakathā* across 19 matching segments [DharmaNexus]. SuttaCentral records five modern translations in five languages [SuttaCentral].
